blocks.name: Moving average
blocks.watches: The average price over a number of bars. Price above it usually means an uptrend; below it, a downtrend.

settings.label: Bars
settings.help: More bars make a slower, smoother line that only shows the big trend.

range.why: an average over fewer than 2 bars is just the price

settings.label: Kind
settings.help: Exponential reacts faster to recent prices; simple weighs every bar the same.

ports.words: the price is above its {ma_type} average over {period:bars}
the price is below its {ma_type} average over {period:bars}

blocks.name: Average crossover
blocks.watches: Two averages, a fast one and a slow one. Fast above slow means the trend is up; the moment they cross is when the trend changes.

settings.label: Fast (bars)
settings.help: Fewer bars react sooner, but give more false starts.

settings.label: Slow (bars)
settings.help: The longer-term trend the fast average is compared with.

range.why: an average over fewer than 2 bars is just the price

settings.label: Kind
settings.help: Exponential reacts faster to recent prices; simple weighs every bar the same.

ports.words: the average over {fast_period:bars} is above the one over {slow_period:bars}
the average over {fast_period:bars} is below the one over {slow_period:bars}
the average over {fast_period:bars} crosses above the one over {slow_period:bars}
the average over {fast_period:bars} crosses below the one over {slow_period:bars}

blocks.name: RSI
blocks.watches: How hard the price has been pushed one way lately, from 0 to 100. Very low means it fell hard (oversold); very high means it rose hard (overbought).

settings.label: Bars to look at
settings.help: Fewer bars give a quicker, jumpier reading. 2 is very short-term.

range.why: an RSI over fewer than 2 bars only reads 0 or 100

settings.label: Oversold below
settings.help: Lower means fewer, more extreme dips count.

range.why: an RSI only reads between 0 and 100

settings.label: Overbought above
settings.help: Higher means fewer, more extreme spikes count.

range.why: an RSI only reads between 0 and 100

ports.words: RSI({rsi_period}) is below {oversold}
RSI({rsi_period}) is above {overbought}
RSI({rsi_period}) is back to 50 or higher
RSI({rsi_period}) is back to 50 or lower

blocks.name: Stretch from average
blocks.watches: How far the price has strayed from its average, measured in its normal wobble (standard deviations), with RSI as a second opinion. Prices that stray far often snap back.

settings.label: Average over (bars)
settings.help: The average the stretch is measured from.

range.why: a spread over fewer than 2 bars is always zero

settings.label: Stretch to enter
settings.help: In normal wobbles. Higher means only bigger stretches count.

settings.label: Stretch to give up
settings.help: If it stretches this far instead of snapping back, the trade closes.

settings.label: RSI bars
settings.help: The bars RSI looks at for its second opinion.

range.why: an RSI over fewer than 2 bars only reads 0 or 100

settings.label: RSI oversold
settings.help: RSI has to be below this to buy.

range.why: an RSI only reads between 0 and 100

settings.label: RSI overbought
settings.help: RSI has to be above this to sell short.

range.why: an RSI only reads between 0 and 100

ports.words: the price is more than {entry_z_threshold} standard deviations below its average over {ma_period:bars} and RSI({rsi_period}) is below {rsi_oversold}
the price is more than {entry_z_threshold} standard deviations above its average over {ma_period:bars} and RSI({rsi_period}) is above {rsi_overbought}
the price is back up to its average over {ma_period:bars}, or falls more than {stop_z_threshold} standard deviations below it
the price is back down to its average over {ma_period:bars}, or rises more than {stop_z_threshold} standard deviations above it

blocks.name: Breakout channel
blocks.watches: The highest high and lowest low of recent bars. Breaking above that high, or below that low, is a classic breakout.

settings.label: Breakout over (bars)
settings.help: More bars mean only bigger breakouts count, so fewer trades.

settings.label: Exit over (bars)
settings.help: Fewer bars exit sooner when the move fades.

ports.words: the price breaks above its {entry_period:bars} high
the price breaks below its {entry_period:bars} low
the price breaks below its {exit_period:bars} low
the price breaks above its {exit_period:bars} high

blocks.name: Noise band
blocks.watches: How far the price usually moves from the US open by this time of day. Moving past that usual range suggests a real move, not noise. Intraday bars only.

settings.label: Sessions to average
settings.help: More sessions make a steadier band.

settings.label: Band width ×
settings.help: Wider means only bigger breakouts count.

ports.words: the price breaks above the noise band (the usual move from the open, over the last {lookback_sessions} sessions)
the price breaks below the noise band (the usual move from the open, over the last {lookback_sessions} sessions)
the price falls back below the band or the day's average price (VWAP)
the price rises back above the band or the day's average price (VWAP)
the US session ends (16:00 New York)

blocks.stop: the other side of the noise band

blocks.name: MACD
blocks.watches: The gap between a fast and a slow average (MACD), and a smoothed copy of it (the signal line). MACD crossing above its signal line means momentum is turning up.

settings.label: Fast
settings.help: Bars for the fast average.

settings.label: Slow
settings.help: Bars for the slow average.

range.why: an average over fewer than 2 bars is just the price

settings.label: Signal
settings.help: Bars to smooth MACD into its signal line. Fewer reacts sooner.

range.why: a signal line over fewer than 2 bars is the line itself, so the two never cross

ports.words: MACD is above its signal line
MACD is below its signal line
MACD crosses above its signal line
MACD crosses below its signal line

blocks.name: Momentum
blocks.watches: Whether the price is higher or lower than it was a number of bars ago.

settings.label: Bars back
settings.help: More bars look at a longer-term direction.

ports.words: the price is higher than {lookback:bars} ago
the price is lower than {lookback:bars} ago

blocks.name: Trend strength (ADX)
blocks.watches: How strong the current trend is, from 0 to 100, whichever way it points. Above about 25 is a real trend; below it the price is mostly drifting sideways. Use it with a block that says which way.

settings.label: Bars
settings.help: Fewer bars react sooner but jump around more.

range.why: an ADX over fewer than 2 bars is only ever 0 or 100

settings.label: Strong trend at
settings.help: Higher means only the strongest trends count.

range.why: an ADX only reads between 0 and 100

ports.words: there's a strong trend (ADX at {threshold} or more)
there's no strong trend (ADX below {threshold})

blocks.name: Bollinger bands
blocks.watches: A band around the average price, as wide as the price's normal wobble. Closing outside the band means it has stretched further than usual; the middle line is the average it often returns to.

settings.label: Bars
settings.help: The average and the wobble are measured over this many bars.

range.why: a spread over fewer than 2 bars is always zero

settings.label: Band width
settings.help: In normal wobbles (standard deviations). Wider means only bigger stretches count.

settings.label: Squeeze over (bars)
settings.help: A squeeze is the band at its narrowest in this many bars: a quiet spell that often ends in a big move. About six months of daily bars is the usual.

range.why: the narrowest band over 1 bar is always the current one

settings.label: Squeeze in the last (bars)
settings.help: Leave empty to skip. Set it to use "squeezed recently": the squeeze held on any of this many bars, so it still counts on the bar that breaks out, when the band has already started to widen. Pair it with a close outside the band.

range.why: a squeeze in the last 0 bars never fires

ports.words: the price closes below its lower Bollinger band ({std_dev_mult} normal wobbles under its average over {period:bars})
the price closes above its upper Bollinger band ({std_dev_mult} normal wobbles over its average over {period:bars})
the price is back up to its average over {period:bars}
the price is back down to its average over {period:bars}
the Bollinger bands (over {period:bars}) are the narrowest in {squeeze_lookback:bars}: a squeeze
the Bollinger bands (over {period:bars}) were squeezed, the narrowest in {squeeze_lookback:bars}, at some point in the last {squeeze_within:bars|1}

blocks.name: Stochastic
blocks.watches: Where the price closed within its recent high-to-low range, from 0 (at the low) to 100 (at the high), plus a smoothed copy of that line. Near the bottom of its range for a while often means it's stretched down.

settings.label: Bars
settings.help: The range is the high and low of this many bars.

settings.label: Smoothing
settings.help: Bars to average into the second line. More is smoother but slower.

range.why: a signal line over fewer than 2 bars is the line itself, so the two never cross

settings.label: Oversold below
settings.help: Lower means fewer, more extreme dips count.

range.why: the stochastic only reads between 0 and 100

settings.label: Overbought above
settings.help: Higher means fewer, more extreme spikes count.

range.why: the stochastic only reads between 0 and 100

ports.words: the stochastic (where the price sits in its {period:bars} range) is below {oversold}
the stochastic (where the price sits in its {period:bars} range) is above {overbought}
the stochastic (where the price sits in its {period:bars} range) crosses above its smoothed line
the stochastic (where the price sits in its {period:bars} range) crosses below its smoothed line

blocks.name: Opening range
blocks.watches: The high and low of the first minutes after the US open (09:30 New York). Breaking out of that early range often sets the direction for the day. Intraday bars only.

settings.label: First minutes
settings.help: Longer makes a wider range, so fewer but bigger breakouts. 5 with 5-minute bars makes the range the first bar alone.

settings.label: First breakout only
settings.help: Yes: only the day's first close outside the range counts, so a breakout trades at most once a day. If another rule blocks that first one, nothing trades later that day.

reads.text: for the first time that day

settings.label: No new trades in the last (minutes)
settings.help: Leave empty for no limit. 0 stops a trade opening on the closing bar itself; 15 stops any in the last quarter hour. Closing a trade is never blocked.

range.why: a negative guard never blocks anything, the same as none

reads.text: , but not in the last {} minutes before the close
, but not on the closing bar

ports.words: the price breaks above the high of the first {minutes} minutes after the US open{first_breakout_only}{no_entry_before_close}
the price breaks below the low of the first {minutes} minutes after the US open{first_breakout_only}{no_entry_before_close}
the price is still inside the range of the first {minutes} minutes after the US open
the US session ends (16:00 New York)
the first {minutes} minutes after the US open end above the 09:30 open (decided as they end){no_entry_before_close}
the first {minutes} minutes after the US open end below the 09:30 open (decided as they end){no_entry_before_close}

blocks.stop: the other side of the opening range (its low for a buy, its high for a short)

blocks.name: Calm or wild
blocks.watches: How big the bars have been lately compared with how big they usually are. Some strategies only work in calm markets, others only when things are moving.

settings.label: Recent (bars)
settings.help: How many recent bars count as now.

settings.label: Usual (bars)
settings.help: How many bars set what's usual.

range.why: the usual range needs more than 1 bar

ports.words: the market is calmer than usual (the last {period:bars} compared with the last {baseline:bars})
the market is wilder than usual (the last {period:bars} compared with the last {baseline:bars})

series.label: Bar size now vs usual (% of price)

blocks.name: Day's average price (VWAP)
blocks.watches: The average price everyone has paid today since the US open, weighted by how much traded. Big traders watch it: above it, buyers are in control; below it, sellers are. Intraday bars only.

ports.words: the price is above the day's average price (VWAP)
the price is below the day's average price (VWAP)

blocks.name: Pivot points
blocks.watches: Price levels worked out from the previous session's high, low and close: a middle pivot, a resistance level above it (R1) and a support level below (S1). Traders watch them as places the price may stall or turn.

ports.words: the price is above the pivot (from the previous session's high, low and close)
the price is below the pivot (from the previous session's high, low and close)
the price is above the first resistance level (R1)
the price is below the first support level (S1)

blocks.name: Interest-rate carry
blocks.watches: The gap between the two currencies' central-bank interest rates, as it stood on each day. Holding the higher-rate currency against the lower one earns the gap, so money tends to flow that way. Currency pairs only.

settings.label: Smallest gap (points)
settings.help: In percentage points a year. A smaller gap counts as level and signals neither way. OANDA keeps about 1 point a year, so below that a position pays more than it earns.

range.why: below 0 a long and a short would both fire on the same carry

ports.words: the first currency's central-bank rate is at least {min_spread} percentage points above the second's (holding it earns)
the first currency's central-bank rate is at least {min_spread} percentage points below the second's (selling it short earns)

blocks.name: Event window
blocks.watches: Whether the next bar falls inside a window around a scheduled announcement, such as a central-bank decision.

ports.words: it's inside the event window
it's outside the event window
